I rarely put reviews. But this one needs it i feel

I got the game due to a friend talking of it. We tried playing it together, we had fun. Then like always cause i'm the try harder of our group, i went on and started to play solo to try to finish the game once with every character.

I see many says the game is too hard to win solo. I say, you just have to learn how the game works. Get used to the gameplay, find your comfort weapons and all and you'll succeed. Right now, i finished with 3 of the 4 characters in solo.

Overall, the game is plenty of fun, you can make crazy builds, it's fast paced, looks very nice and it is smooth to play. A bit of a spike on the second level due to the increase of ennemies health and damage while you lack still some items to deal high damage.

Devs clearly love their game and i hope to keep seeing that game rank up and reach new heights. I hope next update will add more missions though

A solid enough Risk of Rain-like, that my friends and I have actually ended up comparing to the Dani classic "Muck" a fair bit more than we'd expected to. Obnoxious millennialisms in the writing aside, I also vibe with the atmosphere well enough — a bright world with funky lil character designs, and visual effects that (mostly) don't turn the whole thing into the kind of chaotic mess that I've come to expect from most Risk of Rain-likes

Also: it runs alright, though the art direction honestly doesn't offer much of a difference in fidelity across the whole range of settings. imo: just set everything low, and take all the frames that you can get. Expect about a 30% drop in frames by the end of each level, as the hordes [i]really[/i] intensify

I strongly believe that many of the people who are saying that LORT is too hard have a Risk of Rain 2 mindset when starting a run. You will be SEVERELY punished for not spending as much time as you can in each area looting your ass off. Faster does not equal easier in LORT. The enemies are still challenging even if you collect every single item you can but the difficulty is nowhere near approaching unfun territory.
     What's very refreshing about this gem is that it's very hard to be able to break the game like in most roguelite/likes (at least for me it is :3). The comedy hits, the music slaps, and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ do I love Stewart.
     Most of my critiques come from LORT still being in early access. small gripes that will obviously be worked on as time passes.
     I would easily put this in my top 3 roguelikes right up there with Hades and RoR2. This game seriously rocks and I'm hyped to see what the devs are cooking.

EDIT: I revoke my statement about Astrid being trash. Apologies I was too butt at the game to realize her glory...

Feedback so far, after 50 hours:
1. My main concern is CO-OP. When I queue up with a friend who is playing a character with a different main stat, I basically get grieved. Not intentionally, however, if I focus my main stat and my friend focuses their main stat then we're practically playing solo. When I'm playing solo, I manage to get out of the first region having around 15-17 main stat comfortably. Meanwhile, when playing with a friend (duo), I manage 10 on a REALLY good day. The sub-stats are never significant enough to make up for the difference. Please look into this, it may not be a bigger issue when playing in parties of 8, but it definitely is in a party of 2.

2. Revive mechanic is very impractical. During a boss fight, standing still for longer than 2 seconds pretty much means death, let alone the horrendously long time it takes to revive a teammate. I suggest using a gauge system to revive teammates, which gets filled up through attacking boss or such.

3. Allow us to choose starting weapon (Regardless of class).

4. Allow us to change crosshair.

5. Permanent markers in case of finding a valuable shop and not having money at the time of finding.
reviews.developer_response: Hey turk. A lot of your desires are ours as well like starting weapons, crosshairs, and making Ping better/permanent. We also need to do a bit more experience shaping per your first point. Thanks for the review!

Like most other people are saying, there's basically negative scaling for your characters and infinite scaling for enemies so by level 3 everything is a complete bullet sponge that also 1 shot you. Risk of Rain 2 is a somewhat close game to compare to except this game has no re-rolling, selling, recycling, or anything to change your build, you're just stuck with what you get. There's 2 weapons per class, they only level up flat stats... 

Nighttime on anything past level 2 is just run away constantly or you'll instantly die. Right when you finally start to think, "oh I'm getting kinda powerful, fun!" you go into the next round and it's like you're level 1, or worse, again. Gold is always in extreme short supply so even though there's a million chests, you can only open maybe 5 of them per round. Gold weirdly doesn't carry between rounds, so spend what you got. 

Our whole group feels like "what am I even supposed to do?" by round 3. If the answer is to hardcore grind to build passive stats, then I'm out because that's insanely boring. This game has good bones, that's why I'm writing this review. I want to like this game and it's close to that, but if the devs don't realize hard mechanics are fun, bullet sponges are not, then this game isn't going to get there.

A fun little looting-and-shooting fantasy roguelike that doesn't take itself too seriously. Like Megabonk, except you have to actually aim and fire your abilities. Pretty decent game, not at all bad for the price, if you grab it on sale. It was pretty rough at launch, but development has come a good ways since.

The most recent update seems to have taken a big stride toward addressing a lot of my biggest issues with the game from before - the ability to customize your build has been greatly improved with increased choices for powerups and attributes, there is now an actual variety of weapons that are viable, and you have a better opportunity to upgrade your weapons before you have to face the boss/move to the next level. Single-player balance could still use a bit of work imo, but at least the rest of the game is in much better shape now.

The difficulty scaling makes this game a slog, not fun, even in multiplayer. Bosses are absolute dps sponges. The world seems very empty when you're hunting for power up POIs against the in-game 3 day timer. There aren't enough power ups or interesting/meaningful items, the stat boosts you get from items are so small they don't have any fundamental impact on your power level. The cost for unlocks using rune juice is stupidly overpriced for the benefits they actually give. 

I think the demo was balanced better with mob difficulty than the current version. There are many many many other games in this genre that do it better and respect your time/grind. I think there's a good game here but not in the current state.

reviews.review:
It's quite fun  but...

The game is definitely geared towards multiplayer because the second map is extremely difficult playing solo. You need to kill 2 mini bosses then fight the boss. It's takes up a lot of time jsut to get to the 2 mini bosses then to the final boss.  As for the first map, you can easily defeat the boss solo but it will take you a good 5-10 mins to defeat it because no matter how many power ups and stats upgrades you get, you won't dish out enough damage. 

Next, the movement is quite odd. Most of the time in a heated battle, i can't even tell if i'm sprinting. That's how similar sprinting and normal moving is. Getting places to places takes too long. Even if you use the flowers to propel you, they aren't always facing where you want to go. Meaning you can't realistcally hit all the towns and totems. 

Dodge is useless. the 3 seconds that is needed should be changed to 1 second. You can simply move out of the way of most attacks. 

Not enough item variety. I've been getting the same weapons every run and almost the same power ups. I wish there were more.

LORT with boys or be left behind! Simple to start, harder to master. Thumbs up.
